title: Deterministic cohort allocator and rapid-autorevert A/B framework
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a lightweight, deterministic cohort allocation and rapid-autorevert framework for running A/B and canary model experiments. The goal is to enable low-friction experiments (canaries, small A/B splits, shadow validation) with clear safety budgets, deterministic bucketing, sequential statistical checks, and a configurable auto-rollback path for critical regressions.

Background & motivation:
- Teams currently implement ad-hoc A/B bucketing or rely on broader rollout controls; this leads to inconsistent cohorts, difficulty reproducing failures, and slow reaction to regressions.
- We want an in-platform primitive that guarantees deterministic cohort assignment (by user_id/request_id), sticky routing, resource-aware shadowing, and baked-in early-fail detection.
- This should integrate with the Console dashboards and runtime routing so customers can run fast canaries without writing custom code.

Goals:
- Deterministic bucketing by stable key (user_id/device_id/session_id) and experiment id.
- Support: canary (incremental exposure), A/B (N-way splits), holdout cohorts, and shadow-only traffic.
- Exposure budget primitives: max_daily_exposure, cumulative_quota, and time-windowed caps.
- Sequential statistical monitoring (optional SPRT or Bayesian sequential) with configurable alpha/beta and minimum sample size.
- Auto-rollback triggers for critical metrics with operator overrides and audit trail.
- Shadow mode that duplicates requests to variants without impacting response or cost attribution.
- Console UI for experiment creation, quick status, and forced stop/rollback.

Non-goals:
- Full experimentation analytics stack (we will integrate existing telemetry pipelines).
- Complex multi-armed bandit allocation — out of scope for MVP.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Allocation: deterministic hash(key || experiment_id) -> uniform[0,1). Buckets defined as ranges (e.g., 0-0.001 for 0.1%). Hash versioned at experiment creation to ensure reproducible cohorts across rollouts.
2) Sticky assignment: store cohort in routing layer cookie or token (TTL configurable). On subsequent requests the same cohort is used even if experiment config changed, unless user is explicitly evicted.
3) Exposure controls: experiment config has fields: initial_pct, steps (list of {pct, duration}), max_daily_exposure, quota_id. The router enforces real-time quota checks and drops or routes to fallback when budget exhausted.
4) Shadowing: request copy is sent to a shadow endpoint. Shadow flows are tagged to avoid double-billing; shadow logs return values, latency, and token usage to a dedicated shadow telemetry pipeline.
5) Statistical checks: two supported modes:
   - Frequentist sequential: SPRT guard with user-configurable thresholds (alpha, beta, min_n).
   - Bayesian sequential: compute posterior for metric delta; trigger if posterior(prob delta < -threshold) > p_crit.
   Multiple-metrics support with FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) option for simultaneous tests.
6) Auto-rollback: if any critical metric crosses the configured stop condition the system automatically flips a rollback action that can either:
   - Remove variant from routing (fast path), or
   - Drain traffic and hold for post-mortem (quiet path).
   All autoreverts require an audit log entry and an incident stub in Console. Manual override with two-step confirmation is supported.

API / Console surface:
- Create experiment (json): name, experiment_id, key_type, cohorts (map of name -> pct), schedule, metrics (primary + secondary list), safety_budget, statistical_mode, stop_conditions, shadow: boolean.
- Quick actions: pause, resume, rollback, advance step.
- Visual: live exposure, cohort counts, metric deltas, p-values / posterior probabilities, and a single-click rollback button.

Metrics & instrumentation (MVP):
- Core metrics to monitor: request_latency_p50/p95/p99, token_usage_per_request, eval_quality_score (customer-provided measure or classifier proxy), fallback_rate, rejection_rate, safety_score (toxic/undesired output classifier), error_rate.
- Telemetry protocol: annotate each routed request with experiment_id and cohort. Export counters and histograms to metrics pipeline with tags {experiment_id, cohort, model_variant, region}.
- Logging: store per-request lightweight debug traces for sampled fails (up to 1k/s total across platform).

Statistical rules (defaults & rationale):
- Minimal sample: 500 observations per cohort or 1 hour, whichever larger for canaries.
- Default mode: Bayesian sequential with weakly informative prior; trigger if posterior(prob delta < 0) > 0.95 for an important negative regression.
- For latency regressions we use relative increase > 20% with p>0.99 as critical.
- For quality metrics use absolute drop > 1.5% and posterior > 0.95.
- Multiple metrics: any metric flagged as critical forces rollback; secondaries generate alert but do not auto-rollback unless explicitly marked critical.

Safety & human-in-the-loop:
- Rollback action will by default be set to automatic for "critical" metrics only. Non-critical detections create an immediate paging alert and mark the experiment as "Blocked".
- Provide a 15-minute cooldown before auto-rollback to allow on-call to investigate; configurable per-experiment.
- All auto actions produce an immutable audit entry and send a structured incident (linkable) to the Console.

Rollout plan (platform):
Phase 1 (MVP, 6 weeks):
- API & deterministic allocator in runtime router (ENG integration).
- Basic Console create/view UI with exposure counters and manual rollback.
- Shadow traffic plumbing and separate telemetry tags.
Phase 2 (6 weeks):
- Sequential monitoring service + simple Bayes/SPRT engine (configurable).
- Auto-rollback wiring + audit logs + incident integration.
Phase 3 (4 weeks):
- FDR correction, multiple-metric dashboards, task-runbook templates, and improved UX for experiment templates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customers can create a canary experiment with deterministic bucketing and reach 10% exposure through staged steps without code changes.
- Shadow mode can be enabled, and shadowed responses recorded in shadow telemetry without affecting live metrics or billing.
- System triggers an auto-rollback when pre-defined critical metric rule is violated under simulated load (integration tests).
- Console shows live cohort counts and metric deltas with <5s update latency for experiments <= 100req/s.

Tasks / implementation backlog:
- Define experiment schema and validation rules (PM/ENG).
- Router: deterministic hashing, sticky cookie/token, and exposure enforcement (ENG-48211).
- Shadow proxy: duplicate requests and tag as shadow (ENG-48677).
- Telemetry: tagging, metrics export, and dashboard endpoints (ENG-49200).
- Monitoring: implement SPRT and Bayesian sequential services (ENG-49512).
- Console: experiment creation UI, live view, and rollback actions (DES-9821, ENG-49999).
- E2E tests & chaos scenarios for rollback correctness (ENG-50120).

Design links and mockups:
- Design brief: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PL/pages/Model+Experiment+Gatekeeper (mock)
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic cohort assignment by key and experiment id
Sticky routing persists cohort across sessions unless evicted
Shadow traffic captured to shadow telemetry without billing double-count
Auto-rollback triggers on critical metric breach in integration test
Console displays live exposure and allows manual override/rollback
tasks: PM: finalize schema and default safety presets
ENG: implement deterministic allocator in router (ENG-48211)
ENG: implement shadow proxy and tagging (ENG-48677)
DES: wire UI for experiment creation and quick rollback (DES-9821)
QA: create e2e tests for autorevert and shadow flows
rollout_plan: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 10% staged increments by default. Each step waits for minimum sample or time window and passes sequential checks before advancing. Autorevert can be immediate for critical metrics or delayed by configured cooldown (default 15m).
risks: False positives in sequential tests causing unnecessary rollbacks
Shadow paths increasing backend load if not rate-limited
Incorrect bucketing changes breaking stickiness on config updates
Metric instrumentation gaps lead to blind spots for critical regressions
notes: We should expose conservative presets for safety-budgeted experiments that match enterprise needs (SLA-conscious). Plan a joint runbook with SRE for autorevert incidents.
